Study: how much shorter can a prediction-powered confidence interval for E[Y] be when the labeled set, the unlabeled set
and the predictor are fixed? (Delivered under `code/` and `results/` of the paper repository; the same files are in
`experiment-repo`.) Result files: `results/README.md` (what each was computed on) and `results/METHODS.md` (definitions of
every method id, interval construction and column).

## Layout
```
src/pci/          library: calibrators.py (g(Z) fits), estimators.py (pooled cross-fitted estimator, PPI/PPI++ via ppi-python,
                  intervals, 1-SE selection), pops.py (real pools, synthetic generators with known truth, floor statistics,
                  shift / non-MCAR / rare-event populations), runner.py (Monte-Carlo driver, resumable cells), analysis.py, paths.py
experiments/      one script per experiment (E1..E7), floors*.py, nstar_ci.py, ballots_native.py, get_data.py
analysis/         build_results.py (all delivered tables), planned.py (planned vs stored cells), sync_delivery.sh
results/          aggregated CSV/JSON/MD (delivered); results/exp*/ raw per-replicate cells (*.npz, not in git; release asset)
```
`results/` is found automatically (`$PCI_RESULTS`, else `<root>/results`, else `<root>/../results`); data in `$PCI_DATA`
(default `/hutian/work/data`).

## Environment
Python 3.11.2; numpy 2.4.6, scipy 1.17.1, pandas 3.0.6, scikit-learn 1.9.1, **ppi-python 0.2.3** (PPI / PPI++ baselines), gdown 6.5.2
(see `requirements.txt`). CPU only. All worker processes are single-threaded (`OMP_NUM_THREADS=1`, set in `experiments/common.py`).

## Data
Nine example sets of `ppi-python==0.2.3` (loader `ppi_py.datasets.load_dataset`, anonymous Google Drive download via `gdown`):
`python experiments/get_data.py` downloads whatever is missing into `$PCI_DATA` and writes `results/data_sha256.txt`
(SHA-256 and array shapes of the files used). Nothing else is downloaded; no model is trained (the supplied `Yhat` is the fixed predictor).

## Seeds
Cell seed = 20261126 + crc32(cell id) mod 10^6 (`experiments/common.py`); replicate r uses `numpy.random.SeedSequence([seed, r])`,
so a cell is reproducible and independent of the number of processes. Bootstrap indices in `analysis/build_results.py` use fixed seeds (0, 1).
Every stored cell records its seed, its replicate count and the code version (git SHA, `+dirty` if the working tree differed) in its meta data.
The estimator code (`src/pci/{calibrators,estimators,pops,runner,analysis}.py`) is unchanged since commit 931cb22, which fixed the arms; later commits add
scripts, `paths.py` and analysis only (`git diff 931cb22 HEAD -- src experiments`).

# Methods behind `results/*.csv`

All numbers are computed by `analysis/build_results.py` from the stored Monte-Carlo cells (`results/exp*/*.npz`, one
cell = one (population, n, N) with R repeated samples; raw cells are published as a release asset, not in git) and
from the population fits `results/floors.json` / `results/nstar_ci.json`.

## Target and notation
Target: the population mean E[Y]. A sample has n labeled records (Y, Z) and N unlabeled records (Z); M = n + N.
Tier T1: Z = f (the supplied prediction). Tier T2: Z = (f, X). Labels are MCAR with known propensity n/M (a simple
random subset of the M records). Pool-based cells treat the pool as the population (truth = pool mean) and draw
n + N records iid **with replacement** (`sampling = with_replacement`); synthetic populations are drawn iid
(`synthetic_iid`). Per-cell seed = 20261126 + crc32(cell id) mod 10^6; replicate r uses `SeedSequence([seed, r])`.

## Method ids (`method`)
| id | what it is |
|---|---|
| `labels_z`, `labels_t` | labels only: sample mean ± z (or t_{n-1}) × s/√n |
| `labels_wilson`, `labels_cp` | labels only, binary Y: Wilson, Clopper–Pearson (`construction` = `wilson`, `cp`) |
| `ppi` | PPI, λ = 1 (`ppi-python==0.2.3`, `ppi_mean_ci`, its own CLT interval) |
| `ppipp` | PPI++ with tuned λ (`ppi-python==0.2.3`); the baseline of every ratio |
| `strat_ppi` | pooled estimator with g = stratum means over 5 quantile bins of f, cross-fitted (post-stratified PPI, run post hoc) |
| `ppipp_on_iso`, `ppipp_on_spline` | `ppi-python` PPI++ run with Yhat := ĝ(f), ĝ = cross-fitted isotonic / spline (nearest published-plus-calibration comparator) |
| `pooled_linear` | pooled cross-fitted estimator with g = OLS line of Y on f; algebraically PPI++ with λ = b̂N/M up to cross-fitting (E2 checks this) |
| `calib_spline` | **instrument**: pooled cross-fitted estimator, g = cubic B-spline of f (5 quantile knots, df = 7) |
| `calib_iso` | same with g = isotonic regression of Y on f |
| `select` | headline T1 arm: among linear / spline / isotonic keep the linear g unless another lowers the cross-fitted mean squared residual by more than 1 standard error of the paired difference (1-SE safeguard); selection is inside the replicate loop on the same folds as the SE. `selectmin` = plain argmin of the residual variance (no safeguard) |
